Two independent renderings inside one deposit agree on every code. The Qualtrics exports' first row names each PANAS_n column's adjective and carries the shared stem verbatim; materials_PANAS20.pdf numbers the same twenty adjectives 1-20 in the same order and prints the five anchors. A data-side check confirms the PDF's scoring key: with PA = 1,3,5,9,10,12,14,16,17,19, every adjective correlates more strongly with its own block than with the other (within .45 and .48, between -.16). NOT ESTABLISHED: nothing material.

The deposit's Appendix 1 prints all twelve items in Polish and English but labels them DT_1..DT_12 while the data call them ZR_1..ZR_12. Two things close that gap. The deposit's own analysis code writes '# moved DT_2' directly above the model that moves ZR_2. And the three factors that code fits group the ZR codes exactly as the appendix's item CONTENT groups them -- the kooperacja four (ZR_4, 6, 8, 11) are the four peer-relations items and the misfit the author moved, ZR_2, is itself a peer item. Direction: the appendix scores A = 1, B = 0 with six items marked reverse, and all twelve item-total correlations are positive in the data, which raw A/B coding cannot produce, so resp 1 always means the task is attained and option_text follows that per item. zr_cleaned.rda reproduces all 16,308 live rows. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether 'Zycie szkolne jest:' is a stem for every item or only the first; the appendix prints it once in the table's header row, so it ships as a shared section_prompt with item_text blank.

No mapping step -- item_1..item_4 are the data frame's own columns -- and data(Abortion) reproduces all eight live item x resp cells exactly (1,516 rows against 1,516). The package does not label 0 and 1, so the direction was read off the endorsement pattern: item_1 ('the woman decides on her own') is the only item below .5 at .438 against .594-.636 for the other three, which is the ordering the 1986 British Social Attitudes data is known for, so resp 1 is 'the law should allow it'. NOT ESTABLISHED: the Yes/No labels are this project's rendering of the stem, not the package's; and ?Abortion prints item 1 as an incomplete sentence, shipped unaltered.
